description.narrative:
The objective of this project is to rehabilitate and empower 20-girls affected by obstetric fistula with self-confidence and entrepreneurship skills needed for them to improve the quality of their livelihood and fulfill their potential. Obstetric fistulais a pregnancy and Childbirth complication caused by prolonged obstructed labor. Its the most devastating and serious of all childbirth injuries. Obstetric fistula leaves a teenage girl/woman with a rupture between her birth canal and bladder, rendering her incontinent of urine, feces, or both. On top of the trauma of living with fistula, many Ugandans regard the condition as a curse, and as such survivors are often abandoned by their families and ostracized by their communities, forcing survivors to livealone, cut off from supportsystems. In Uganda the National Obstetric Fistula Strategy of 2012-2016 estimated up to 200,000 Ugandan women suffering from obstetric fistula and about 1,900 new cases each year. In this project, we shall conduct a social vulnerability assessment of the affectedgirls and select 20-Rights holders to participate in the empowerment program. The assessment will focus on systems of oppression women might be dealing with in their rural communities including poverty, homelessness,and physical, economic, psychological, or emotional abuse. The selected 20 - Rights holders (Fistula survivors) will receive an empowerment training tailored to respond to their current needs such as psychosocial support, income generating activity, leadership and human rights skills.
Specifically, the objectives of the project are; • To build a network of 20 – Rights holders (Sister friends) who are living positively and recovering from fistula, to create an environment for psychosocial support for complete holistic healing from the societal stigma and trauma. • To support each girl participating in the project to ideate, identify and create income- generating activities that they are passionate about and are able to startup, so as to increase their chances of acquiring descent employment to improve the quality of their livelihoods. • To develop community change Agents (Leaders) for awareness creation, lobbying and advocacy about obstetric fistula in Uganda.
The change we want to see; • Rightsholders living positively, fulfilling their potential with a high self esteem, valuing themselves. • Rights holders running successful business, earning income and saving to afford basic education and health for their children • Rights holders who can communicate and express their views without limitation. Able to advocate for their rights.

participating-org.narrative:
Talents Enabling Uganda exists to bridge the high unemployment gap by supporting disadvantaged youth and women discover and translate their talents, passions, skills and abilities to form income-generating activities to improve the quality of their livelihoods. We do this through training, coaching and mentoring groups of these individuals in communities to ideate, start-up and run sustainably businesses.
• In 2016, we piloted our programs of training both in and out of school youth in self-discovery and support them translate their ideas into business. This was meant to help us identify good practises and good approached that we can use. This led to development of ARISE-Acceleration program; where would enrol 40-youths in January of every year, takethem through a one weeks boot-camp in self discovery and then mentor them for six month in business development. The output of our pilot was 148 youth trained. •In 2018, we instituted the process of developing organizational systems to ensure that we are able to deliver on the programing in the communities in which we serve. We needed good working systems to improve our organizational capacity to deliver. Systems like reports, finance and human resource procedures and standard to be followed by team members. We also put in place a Governance system where we got a board to advice us and keep us in check. • Within 2018, when we discovered in our pilot that young people who were in school were not able to commit for the acceleration program; we decided tofocus on out-of school youths and also added hands-on skills in the trainings. This is when we got our first partner organization (TERREWODE) who sponsored part of the program and also gave us 20-girls to train. It was also a year when we started integrating gender into our programs because the partner was particular about Gender. • In 2020 – 2022, We got into a partnership with Mercy-corps. Where we trained 215-urban refugees and vulnerable community members in business plan development and business model canvas. It was also at this stage when we had to strengthen our gender integration. We had to ensure that more than 50% are female in the program. • In 2021 we got a training of Trainers program with ILO totrain in SIYB(Start and Improve your business) and GET-Ahead ( Gender Entrepreneurship Training Approach) • We developed a financial literacy tool kit for training in finance and business management skills. As a result we pivoted in Business Development Services for our vulnerable communities. With an aim to improve involvement in descent employment activities. • From 2022, we started to prepare to scale and learn how to measure growth or results among our beneficiaries. We believe that with the systems in place, we need to grow to the impact level. Being part of this empowerment program gives us much joy because we shall learn as much as we can to grow for both us as the organization and the beneficiaries.
• In 2020 through to 2022, working under the Urban Refugee Response Program in partnership with Mercy corps Uganda, we provided tailored mentorship to 215 urban refugees (Youth and women) in micro businessmanagement. Through this program we saw refugees start their own small and medium business in mechanic, urban farming, detergent amongothers. For example, Jenifer a refugee from Makindye division in Kampala, started a cosmetic shop because she loved fashion and beauty, she makes sales of more than 35$ a day and has joined saving groups. She is able to take care of her self and siblingsschool fees in Uganda. They are no longer depended on Mercy corps for food rations and hand-outs • Through Our flagship business Development model, in 2016 through to 2019, we have trained, coached and mentored 167-youth to discover and start their own business that theyare passionate about. Robert one of the participants, start a detergents making business and now has made shop at Mukono district, employed two other young people to work with him. He has been able to sustain the business beyond the business mortality rates in Uganda. • Jonathan, a young person who had given up on his life, attended our training on self-discovery in 2020 and realized that he has a mission here on earth, decided to go back to school. Till today he is in touch with us and hope that he will one day he will become a businessman. He is passionate an enthusiastic a bout life. • We have partnership with Mercy Corps, TEREWODE, Mercy for Life and St Eliza health Care to provide financial literacy training for their beneficiaries.Lucy from Mercy for life organization joinedour training, she discovered that her limitation is not from outside. She started to save money by becoming disciplined in her expenditures. She saved money and invested in her poultry business, which is growingnow, and we hope that she can reach over 1000 birds. • We have carried out a Business Diagnostics with ECOS project

comment.narrative: TEU supported the formation of 4 groups of rightholders participating in lobbying meetings with duty bearers such as police, local councils, and probation offices to speak about their issues. The formed 4 groups of 5-members each because TEU targeted towork with 20-rightholders throughout the entire project, the impact was evident. Rightsholders in the 4 groups participated in Radio talk shows and at the subcounty budget conference workshop. The groups participated at the community declaration for protection of women and girls, at the event two-rights holders voiced their demands for protection and education duty bearers such as police, local councils, and probation offices to speak about their issues.

comment.narrative: The Rightsholders joined sister friends clubs for connecting with each other and building of confidence. TEU has been a significant change in confidence of the girls by ways of expression of their views in groups sharing, in being able to talk to the community leaders and being assertive about the issues that affect them and other girls. Within the 4-groups formed, Rightsholders are attending sisterhood community clubs through which they continue engaging in various advocacy efforts.
